name: The Breeders
label: 4AD
lede: Kim Deal started a side project on a Pixies tour, handed lead guitar to a twin sister who had never played one, and wrote Cannonball. Thirty years on, the Last Splash four were opening for Olivia Rodrigo at Madison Square Garden.

eras.title: Two bands' worth of spare songs
eras.text: Kim Deal was writing more songs than Pixies would ever use, and Tanya Donelly of Throwing Muses was in the same spot. They turned it into a band with a joke name, a demo that charmed 4AD's boss, and one week in an Edinburgh studio with Steve Albini.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Breeders · Wikipedia: Kim Deal
years.h: Kim Deal and Tanya Donelly plot a side project on tour
years.p: On a 1988 European tour where Pixies and Throwing Muses shared the bill, Deal and Donelly talk about a band of their own. Deal reuses the name of a teenage folk duo she had with her twin, Kelley.
years.xp: Deal liked the name because it was funny: "breeders" is gay slang for straight people. She also loved horror films, and has pointed to David Cronenberg's 1979 film The Brood.

q: This is absolutely magical, beautiful stuff.
years.h: "Boston Girl Super-Group" plays the Rathskeller once
years.p: With violinist Carrie Bradley and a rotating set of drummers including [[David Narcizo|dcdb6fb6-aa8f-456f-a575-f08c5892b656]], Deal and Donelly cut demos and play a single Boston show under that billing.
years.xp:
Early songs on the tapes included Lime House, Doe and Only in 3's. Ray Halliday played bass; Mickey Bones and Carl Haarer took turns on drums.

4AD's [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]] heard the demo and gave the band an $11,000 budget for an album.

years.h: Two weeks booked in Edinburgh. Pod takes one
years.p: After a week of rehearsals at [[Josephine Wiggs|a9b85146-e796-4b40-90f6-5c1fc7d8e91b]]'s house in Bedfordshire, the band records at Palladium studio with Albini engineering. [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]]'s [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]] drums under the name Shannon Doughton.
years.xp:
Wiggs had met Deal when her band, [[The Perfect Disaster|6d7e05e9-3090-4e79-8747-6a6ad621cf92]], supported Pixies in London in 1988. Walford took the alias so the record wouldn't pull attention from Slint.

Albini cared more about the sound of a live take than about getting every note right, and the band finished in half the time it had booked.

years.h: Pod comes out with a man in a belt of dead eels on the cover
years.p: [[Vaughan Oliver|2a1b1665-17fc-4ad2-9392-d6fe6788e96e]] designed the sleeve and is the dancer in Kevin Westenberg's photo, wearing the eels as a fertility charm. Pod reaches No. 22 in the UK.
years.xp: The cover of the Beatles' Happiness Is a Warm Gun was Watts-Russell's idea. The New York Times's Karen Schoemer heard angular melodies, shattered tempos and screeching dynamics. Pitchfork later put it at No. 81 among the '90s' best albums.

years.h: Two London shows, and the Pod line-up is done
years.p: Deal, Donelly, Wiggs and Walford play London twice in 1990. It's the only time those four share a stage.

eras.title: A twin, a cannonball and a platinum record
eras.text: Kelley Deal came in on guitar with no experience, Donelly left for Belly, and Pixies fell apart in early 1993. That left Kim Deal's side project as her main band just as Cannonball hit MTV.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kelley Deal · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Kelley Deal joins on guitar without ever having played one
years.p: [[Kelley Deal|e146c5fd-1155-4cd4-a228-bb2cda0f341b]], Kim's identical twin, was working as a defence contractor at an Air Force base. She comes in as third guitarist.
years.xp: The twins grew up in Dayton, Ohio, and as teenagers played biker bars, Kim on guitar and both of them singing Hank Williams songs. In 1986 Kim paid for Kelley to audition as Pixies' drummer in Boston; Kelley wasn't confident on drums and preferred Kim's songs anyway.

years.h: Safari is the one record with both Kelley and Donelly
years.p: Four songs, including the Who's So Sad About Us. Walford drums on most of it as "Mike Hunt"; Spiritualized's Jon Mattock plays on the title track.
years.xp: Sessions ran between Looking Glass in New York and First Protocol in London. Robert Christgau gave it an A-minus. The same year Kurt Cobain told Melody Maker the way the Breeders structured songs was totally unique; he later listed Pod among the 50 albums most important to [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Tanya Donelly · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Tanya Donelly leaves to make Belly her main band
years.p: Donelly had formed [[Belly|c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2]] in December 1991; after Safari she goes full time. Walford leaves too, and Kelley becomes the only lead guitarist.

years.cap: The Breeders in Sausalito, California, March 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Last Splash · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Kim Deal sings Last Splash in the studio toilet
years.p: [[Jim Macpherson|68f49f22-f8c9-41fa-920b-dcd04807a9f3]] of Dayton's Raging Mantras takes the drums. At Coast Recorders in San Francisco, the bathroom's echo wins the vocal booth job.
years.xp: Deal co-produced with Mark Freegard. The sessions ran about four months across Coast Recorders and Brilliant Studios in San Francisco and Refraze in Dayton, with mixing at the Record Plant in Sausalito.

years.cap: The Last Splash line-up in New York, June 1993
years.h: Cannonball opens with Kim Deal shouting into a harmonica mic
years.p: The song started as a demo called Grunggae. Wiggs's bass riff carries it; [[Kim Gordon|19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184]] and Spike Jonze direct the video, with Kim Deal singing underwater.
years.xp:
The single reached No. 2 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart and No. 44 on the Hot 100, and went gold in the US. In France it ran 30 weeks and peaked at No. 8.

NME, Melody Maker and the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll all named it the best single of 1993. In the video a cannonball rolls through Los Angeles's Miracle Mile while the Deals pick through a dressing room full of clothes.

years.h: Last Splash goes top five in Britain
years.p: No. 5 in the UK and No. 33 in the US. Divine Hammer follows Cannonball, with Richard Kern joining Jonze and Gordon behind the camera.
years.xp: Vaughan Oliver did the art direction again. Pitchfork ranked Last Splash No. 64 of the 1990s in 2003; Spin had it at No. 39, and Rolling Stone put it at No. 293 of all time in 2020.

years.cap: The Breeders at Roseland Ballroom, New York, November 14, 1993
years.h: Nirvana takes the Breeders out on the In Utero tour
years.p: The Breeders support Nirvana on the 1993 tour. Kurt Cobain had been praising Pod in print since 1992.

years.h: Last Splash passes a million in the US
years.p: The RIAA certifies it platinum by June 1994, about ten months after release.

years.cap: Lollapalooza at Sam Boyd Stadium, Las Vegas, July 7, 1994
years.src: Wikipedia: The Breeders · Wikipedia: Josephine Wiggs
years.h: Lollapalooza's Los Angeles stop is the last show for years
years.p: The band spends the summer on Lollapalooza '94. Its Los Angeles date on September 5 turns out to be the last Breeders show of the era.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kelley Deal · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Kelley Deal's heroin arrest stops the band
years.p: Kelley is arrested for heroin possession and spends 1995 in rehab. The Breeders go on indefinite hiatus.
years.xp: Kelley had used heroin since her teens. By February 2018 the New York Times reported she was in her eighth year of sobriety. Kim also went through rehab in the years that followed.

eras.title: Tammy Ampersand and the Kelley Deal 6000
eras.text: With the Breeders parked, both twins made records under other names in Dayton. Kim took the band name back in 1996, but the third album wouldn't come together for six more years.

years.cap: Kim Deal with the Amps in Dayton, Ohio, 1995
years.src: Wikipedia: The Breeders · Wikipedia: Kim Deal
years.h: Kim Deal becomes Tammy Ampersand and makes Pacer
years.p: The Amps are Deal, Macpherson, Luis Lerma of the Tasties and Nate Farley, later of [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]]. Pacer is their one album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kelley Deal · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Kelley starts a band and a label, then a supergroup
years.p: After rehab she forms The Kelley Deal 6000, releasing Go to the Sugar Altar on her Nice Records, and the Last Hard Men with Sebastian Bach, [[Jimmy Chamberlin|48d3d17b-0bb8-44a0-9fb0-23f594bb4df3]] and Jimmy Flemion.
years.xp:
The Kelley Deal 6000 followed with Boom! Boom! Boom! in 1997. Band and label went on hiatus when she rejoined the Breeders.

Meanwhile in New York, Wiggs co-produced the Kostars' Klassics with a K, made a solo album for the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]]' Grand Royal label, and formed Dusty Trails with Vivian Trimble of Luscious Jackson.

years.h: Kim takes back the Breeders name with the Amps
years.p: The Amps plus Carrie Bradley on violin become the Breeders. A 1997 try at a third album doesn't work out.

years.h: One song for The Mod Squad
years.p: The only release from the late-'90s line-up is Collage, a cover of a song recorded by the Three Degrees and the James Gang, on the film's soundtrack.

eras.title: All analog, all Dayton
eras.text: The Deals rebuilt the band with LA punks from Fear and went back to Albini on Kim's terms: tape only, no computers. Two albums came out of it, nine years after Last Splash and then six more.

years.cap: The Breeders at the Water Rats, London, April 24, 2002
years.src: Wikipedia: Title TK · Wikipedia: The Breeders
years.h: Title TK: tape only, no computer editing
years.p: Albini records most of it at Electrical Audio in Chicago between 1999 and 2001. The title is editors' shorthand for "title to come."
years.xp:
Kim called the rule "All Wave" and said it was a reaction to everything sounding so straight and clean. The line-up was Richard Presley and [[Mando Lopez|f59244e4-7a77-47f1-bda3-b22b97612480]], both of Fear, with [[José Medeles|38af1653-52e5-48a6-b323-b12c6b16b1ee]] on drums.

It sold 45,000 copies in the US by June 2004. A Dutch documentary that year, The Breeders: The Real Deal, followed this line-up.

years.h: The Breeders play the Bronze on Buffy the Vampire Slayer
years.p: In the episode "Him" the band performs Little Fury on the show's club stage.

years.h: Pixies reunite, and Kim writes a Breeders song on the road
years.p: Kim Deal rejoins [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]] for their 2004 reunion tour. Walk It Off takes shape on that tour and ends up on the next Breeders album.

years.h: Five years of sessions add up to Mountain Battles
years.p: Recorded from 2002 to 2007 at Electrical Audio, two LA studios, Refraze in Dayton and a basement. It includes a Spanish-language cover, Regalame Esta Noche.
years.xp: Presley had left, so it's the Deals with Lopez and Medeles. Metacritic averaged 75; reviews ran from a C in Entertainment Weekly to 8/10 in NME.

years.h: Mark Lanegan sings on Fate to Fatal
years.p: The EP has [[Mark Lanegan|a9126556-f555-4920-9617-6e013f8228a7]] on The Last Time and a Bob Marley cover. St. Louis's Arch Rival Roller Girls star in the title track's video.

years.cap: Kim Deal on stage at All Tomorrow's Parties, 2009
years.h: The Breeders curate All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead
years.p: They pick the bill at the English holiday camp festival, then curate ATP New York in Monticello in September 2010.

eras.title: The Last Splash four, back for good
eras.text: A 20th-anniversary tour got Wiggs and Macpherson back in a room with the twins. It went well enough that Kim quit Pixies, the four made All Nerve, and the band ended up on arena stages it had never played in the '90s.

years.cap: Playing Last Splash at the 9:30 Club, Washington, D.C., May 4, 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: The Breeders · Wikipedia: Last Splash
yt: LSXX show, El Rey, Los Angeles, Aug 23, 2013
years.h: LSXX brings back Wiggs and Macpherson
years.p: 4AD reissues Last Splash for its 20th anniversary, and the classic line-up tours the US, Europe, Australia and South America, including a [[Deerhunter|4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b]]-curated ATP.

years.h: Kim Deal quits Pixies to concentrate on the Breeders
years.p: She leaves in the middle of the reunion run. By 2023 she said she had no contact with her old Pixies bandmates.

years.h: Wait in the Car arrives on three limited 7-inches
years.p: The first new song from the reunited line-up comes out as three separate singles of 1,500 copies each.

years.h: All Nerve, 25 years after the last album by these four
years.p: Made at Candyland in Dayton, Kentucky, Electrical Audio and Fernwood in Dayton, Ohio. It reaches No. 9 in the UK, higher than anything since Last Splash.
years.xp:
Wiggs stayed at Kim's house in Dayton during sessions instead of making the ten-hour drive from New York. [[Courtney Barnett|55111838-f001-494a-a1b5-9d818db85810]], in town for the Nelsonville Music Festival, sang backing vocals on Howl at the Summit.

Metacritic averaged 84. Mojo put it at No. 10 of 2018.

years.h: A His Name Is Alive cover for 4AD's 40th
years.p: The Breeders record The Dirt Eaters for Bills and Aches and Blues, the label's anniversary covers compilation.

years.h: At Coachella, the Linda Lindas join in
years.p: The Breeders play Coachella with The Linda Lindas joining them.

years.h: Tanya Donelly is back for the encores
years.p: On the Last Splash 30th-anniversary tour, Belly opens some dates and Donelly joins the Breeders for the encore.

years.h: Four nights opening for Olivia Rodrigo at Madison Square Garden
years.p: Kim Deal on [[Olivia Rodrigo|6925db17-f35e-42f3-a4eb-84ee6bf5d4b0]]'s invitation. They open four Garden shows on the Guts tour, then four at the Kia Forum in August.
years.xp:
Deal said it seemed odd at first, until she learned Rodrigo was a fan of Billy Joel and Sheryl Crow and knew St. Vincent: she was just really into music. Billboard's Andrew Unterberger, at the April 8 show, wrote that the band was finally getting to be the arena rockers its '90s records should have made it.

Earlier in 2024 the band supported the [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] in New Zealand.

years.h: Kim Deal's first solo album is out on 4AD
years.p: Nobody Loves You More follows solo singles she started releasing in 2012. Mojo ranks it No. 6 of the year.
